title: Community building: why Sam Parr says start low-friction, run it as a dictatorship, and charge more
summary: Sam Parr explains how he thinks about building paid communities (Hustle Trends, Hampton). He separates an audience from a community, says to launch where people already are, seed it with a leader posting daily, scale slowly and meticulously, and charge more than you think. He backs it all with simple back-of-the-envelope math.

principles.text: If content stops and conversation doesn't continue without you, you have an audience, not a community.
principles.quote: if you quit creating content for like two or three weeks does more conversations happen when you're gone than when you were there if not you have an audience not a community

principles.text: Start a community in the lowest-friction place, where your people already are (Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, Facebook), not a new site or app.
principles.quote: you should start a community in the lowest friction place

principles.text: Seed it by posting daily yourself and getting smart friends to post; real traction took about six months before members commented on their own.
principles.quote: I would post in there every single day for like a year

principles.text: You need a cult-leader-style founder who embodies the culture and is constantly active, setting norms like a CEO would.
principles.quote: you need a leader who embodies it's basically like a cult you need like your cult leader who like embodies like the rituals and the culture

principles.text: Grow slowly and meticulously: let people in deliberately and indoctrinate them with norms, because a community that scales too fast loses its culture.
principles.quote: if it gets too big and and too fast it sucks and there's no culture and there's no soul to it

principles.text: If the community is the business, charge real money, more than you think. Underpricing ($300/yr) forced huge member counts and weaker service.
principles.quote: if you want Community to be the business my opinion you have to charge money and you should probably charge more money than you think
